units.zh: 高谷胡濙王直
units.en: Gao Gu, Hu Ying, and Wang Zhi
units.literal: Gao Gu, Hu Ying, Wang Zhi

units.zh: 高谷，字世用，揚州興化人。
units.en: Gao Gu, courtesy name Shiyong, was from Xinghua in Yangzhou.
units.literal: Gao Gu, styled Shiyong, was a native of Xinghua in Yangzhou.

units.zh: 永樂十三年進士，選庶吉士，授中書舍人。
units.en: In Yongle 13 he passed the metropolitan examination, was chosen as a junior compiler, and was appointed a secretariat drafter.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yongle he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected as a junior compiler, and was appointed Secretariat Drafter.

units.zh: 仁宗即位，改春坊司直郎，尋遷翰林侍講。
units.en: When Renzong succeeded, he was made directing clerk of the Eastern Palace and soon promoted to Hanlin reader-in-waiting.
units.literal: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, he was made Directing Clerk of the Eastern Palace, and soon transferred to Hanlin Reader-in-Waiting.

units.zh: 英宗即位，開經筵，楊士奇薦谷及苗衷、馬愉、曹鼐四人侍講讀。
units.en: When Yingzong opened the Classics Lecture, Yang Shiqi recommended Gao Gu along with Miao Zhong, Ma Yu, and Cao Qi to serve as lecturers and readers.
units.literal: When Emperor Yingzong took the throne and opened the Classics Lecture, Yang Shiqi recommended Gu together with Miao Zhong, Ma Yu, and Cao Qi — four men to serve as lecturers and readers.

units.zh: 正統十年由侍講學士進工部右侍郎，入內閣典機務。
units.en: In Zhengtong 10 he rose from reader-in-waiting academician to right vice minister of works and entered the Grand Secretariat to handle state affairs.
units.literal: In the tenth year of Zhengtong he advanced from Reader-in-Waiting Academician to Right Vice Minister of Works and entered the Grand Secretariat to direct state affairs.

units.zh: 景泰初，進尚書，兼翰林學士，掌閣務如故。
units.en: Early in the Jingtai reign he was promoted to minister while retaining his Hanlin academician post and his former duties in the Grand Secretariat.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Jingtai reign, he was promoted to Minister, also appointed Hanlin Academician, and continued to direct Grand Secretariat affairs as before.

units.zh: 英宗將還，奉迎禮薄，千戶龔遂榮投書於谷，具言禮宜從厚，援唐肅宗迎上皇故事。
units.en: When Emperor Yingzong was due to return, the planned welcome rites were deemed too spare. The qianhu Gong Suirong sent Gao Gu a letter arguing at length that the ceremony should be lavish, invoking Emperor Suzong of Tang welcoming his father home from retirement.
units.literal: When the Ying Emperor was about to return, the welcome ceremony was meager. Qianhu Gong Suirong submitted a letter to Gu, setting forth in detail that the rites ought to be generous, citing the Tang precedent of Emperor Suzong welcoming the retired emperor.

units.zh: 谷袖之入朝，遍示廷臣曰：「武夫尚知禮，況儒臣乎！」
units.en: Gao Gu carried the letter into court hidden in his sleeve and showed it to the ministers, saying, "If even a soldier understands ritual propriety, how much more ought scholar-officials to do so!"
units.literal: Gu tucked it in his sleeve and entered court, showing it round to the court officials, saying: "Even a military man knows propriety — how much more should Confucian ministers!"

units.zh: 眾善其言。
units.en: The officials present agreed that he was right.
units.literal: The assembly approved his words.

units.zh: 胡濙、王直欲以聞。
units.en: Hu Ying and Wang Zhi wanted to bring the matter to the emperor's attention.
units.literal: Hu Ying and Wang Zhi wished to report it to the throne.

units.zh: 谷曰：「迎復議上，上意久不決。
units.en: Gao Gu said, "Memorials on welcoming him back are already before the throne, and the emperor has hesitated for a long time.
units.literal: Gu said: "The proposal to welcome him back has already been submitted, and His Majesty's mind has long been unsettled.

units.zh: 若進此書，使上知朝野同心，亦一助也。」
units.en: If we submit this letter and show him that court and country stand together, that might help move him."
units.literal: If we present this letter and let His Majesty know that court and country are of one mind, that too would be a help."

units.zh: 都御史王文不可。
units.en: The censor-in-chief Wang Wen would not agree.
units.literal: The Censor-in-Chief Wang Wen objected.

units.zh: 已而言官奏之。
units.en: Soon censorial officials memorialized on the matter.
units.literal: Before long the remonstrance officials memorialized about it.

units.zh: 詰所從得，谷對曰：「自臣所。」
units.en: Asked where the letter came from, Gao Gu answered, "From my own hand."
units.literal: When questioned where he obtained it, Gu replied: "From me."

units.zh: 因抗章懇請如遂榮言。
units.en: He then submitted a forceful memorial pleading that the welcome follow Gong Suirong's recommendations.
units.literal: Thereupon he submitted a forthright memorial earnestly asking that matters proceed as Suirong had urged.

units.zh: 帝雖不從，亦不之罪。
units.en: The emperor declined to follow his advice but did not punish him.
units.literal: Though the emperor did not assent, he did not punish him either.

units.zh: 二年進少保、東閣大學士。
units.en: In the second Jingtai year he was made junior guardian and grand secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.
units.literal: In the second year he was advanced to Junior Guardian and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.

units.zh: 易儲，加太子太傅，給二俸。
units.en: When the crown prince was replaced, he was made grand tutor to the heir apparent and granted a double stipend.
units.literal: When the heir was changed, he was given the additional title Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and granted two salaries.

units.zh: 應天、鳳陽災，命祀三陵，振貧民。
units.en: After famine struck Yingtian and Fengyang, he was charged with rites at the three imperial tombs and relief for the destitute.
units.literal: When disasters struck Yingtian and Fengyang, he was ordered to sacrifice at the three imperial tombs and relieve the poor.

units.zh: 七年進謹身殿大學士，仍兼東閣。
units.en: In the seventh year he became grand academician of the Hall of Cultivating Virtue while retaining his Eastern Pavilion post.
units.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted Grand Academician of the Hall of Cultivating Virtue, still concurrently of the Eastern Pavilion.

units.zh: 內閣七人，言論多齟齬。
units.en: The seven grand secretaries often clashed in council.
units.literal: The seven men of the Grand Secretariat were often at odds in debate.

units.zh: 谷清直，持議正。
units.en: Gao Gu was upright in character and steadfast in argument.
units.literal: Gu was pure and upright and held to correct positions in debate.

units.zh: 王文由谷薦，數擠谷。
units.en: Wang Wen owed his rise to Gao Gu's recommendation yet repeatedly tried to undermine him.
units.literal: Wang Wen had been recommended by Gu, yet repeatedly tried to squeeze him out.

units.zh: 谷屢請解機務，不許。
units.en: Gao Gu repeatedly asked to leave state affairs but was not allowed to resign.
units.literal: Gu repeatedly asked to be relieved of administrative duties, but permission was refused.

units.zh: 都給事中林聰忤權要論死，谷力救，得薄譴。
units.en: Chief supervising secretary Lin Cong, who had offended the powerful, was condemned to death; Gao Gu fought hard for him, and Lin escaped with a mild punishment.
units.literal: The Chief Palace Secretary Lin Cong, having offended powerful figures, was sentenced to death; Gu exerted himself to save him, and Lin received only a light reprimand.

units.zh: 陳循及文構考官劉儼、黃諫，帝命禮部會谷復閱試卷。
units.en: Chen Xun and Wang Wen framed the chief examiners Liu Yan and Huang Jian; the emperor ordered the Ministry of Rites, together with Gao Gu, to review the examination papers again.
units.literal: Chen Xun and Wen fabricated charges against the examiners Liu Yan and Huang Jian; the emperor ordered the Ministry of Rites to join with Gu in re-examining the papers.

units.zh: 谷力言儼等無私，且曰：「貴胄與寒士競進，已不可。
units.en: Gao Gu insisted that Liu Yan and his colleagues had shown no favoritism, adding, "It is bad enough when scions of great houses contend with poor scholars for advancement.
units.literal: Gu strongly maintained that Liu and the others were unbiased, and said: "For nobles and poor scholars to compete in advancement is already hard enough.

units.zh: 況不安義命，欲因此構考官乎？」
units.en: Must they also refuse to accept their fate and use this affair to destroy the examiners?"
units.literal: How much worse to be discontent with one's lot in life and try to use this to frame the examiners?"

units.zh: 帝乃賜循、文子中式，惟黜林挺一人，事得已。
units.en: The emperor then allowed the sons of Chen Xun and Wang Wen to pass the examinations, demoting only Lin Ting, and the matter was closed.
units.literal: The emperor thereupon granted Chen Xun's and Wen's sons passage in the examinations, dismissing only Lin Ting, and the affair was closed.

units.zh: 英宗復位，循、文等皆誅竄，谷謝病。
units.en: When Yingzong was restored to the throne, Chen Xun and Wang Wen and their party were put to death or exiled, and Gao Gu retired citing illness.
units.literal: When Emperor Yingzong was restored, Chen Xun, Wen, and the rest were executed or banished, and Gu resigned on grounds of illness.

units.zh: 英宗謂谷長者，語廷臣曰：「谷在內閣議迎駕及南內事，嘗左右朕。
units.en: Yingzong called Gao Gu a man of standing and told the court, "In the Grand Secretariat, on welcoming me home and affairs of the Southern Palace, Gao Gu often stood by me.
units.literal: Emperor Yingzong called Gu a man of maturity and told the court: "When Gu was in the Grand Secretariat and deliberated on welcoming the imperial carriage and matters of the Southern Palace, he often assisted me.

units.zh: 其賜金帛襲衣，給驛舟以歸。」
units.en: He was given gold, silk, and court robes, with an imperial courier boat to take him home."
units.literal: He was granted gold, silks, and ceremonial robes, and given an express boat for his return."

units.zh: 尋復賜敕獎諭。
units.en: Soon after, another edict praised him.
units.literal: Shortly afterward he was again granted an imperial edict of commendation.

units.zh: 谷既去位，杜門絕賓客。
units.en: After leaving office he shut his gates and would see no visitors.
units.literal: Once Gu had left office, he shut his doors and refused guests.

units.zh: 有問景泰、天順間事，輒不應。
units.en: Anyone who asked about events under Jingtai or early Tianshun found him silent.
units.literal: If asked about affairs between the Jingtai and Tianshun reigns, he would not answer.

units.zh: 天順四年正月卒，年七十。
units.en: He died in the first month of Tianshun four, at the age of seventy.
units.literal: In the first month of the fourth year of Tianshun he died, aged seventy.

units.zh: 谷美豐儀，樂儉素，位至臺司，敝廬瘠田而已。
units.en: Gao Gu was imposing in appearance yet loved simplicity; though he reached the highest ministries, he kept only a modest house and meager fields.
units.literal: Gu had a handsome bearing and delighted in plain living; though he rose to high office, he owned only a shabby house and lean fields.

units.zh: 成化初，贈太保，謚文義。
units.en: Early in Chenghua he was posthumously made grand guardian with the posthumous title Wenyi.
units.literal: Early in Chenghua he was posthumously made Grand Guardian and given the posthumous name Wenyi.

units.zh: 胡濙，字源潔，武進人。
units.en: Hu Ying, courtesy name Yuanjie, was from Wujin.
units.literal: Hu Ying, styled Yuanjie, was a native of Wujin.

units.zh: 生而發白，彌月乃黑。
units.en: He was born with white hair, which turned black only after his first month.
units.literal: At birth his hair was white; only after a full month did it turn black.

units.zh: 建文二年舉進士，授兵科給事中。
units.en: In Jianwen two he passed the metropolitan examination and was made a supervising secretary in the military-affairs bureau.
units.literal: In the second year of Jianwen he passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed supervising secretary in the Office for Military Affairs.

units.zh: 永樂元年遷戶科都給事中。
units.en: In Yongle one he was moved to chief supervising secretary in the revenues bureau.
units.literal: In the first year of Yongle he was transferred to chief supervising secretary in the Household Bureau.

units.zh: 惠帝之崩於火，或言遁去，諸舊臣多從者，帝疑之。
units.en: When the Jianwen emperor died in the palace fire, some said he had escaped and that many former officials had gone with him; the Yongle emperor was uneasy.
units.literal: When the Huai Emperor perished in the fire, some said he had escaped, and many old ministers were said to have followed him; the emperor was suspicious.

units.zh: 五年遣濙頒禦制諸書，並訪仙人張邋遢，遍行天下州郡鄉邑，隱察建文帝安在。
units.en: In Yongle five the emperor sent Hu Ying out to distribute imperial works and to search for the immortal Zhang Guaiya, touring every province and village in the land while secretly trying to learn whether the Jianwen emperor was still alive.
units.literal: In the fifth year he dispatched Ying to distribute imperially authored books and also to seek the immortal Zhang Guaiya, traveling through all prefectures, districts, and townships of the empire while secretly investigating where the Jianwen emperor might be.

units.zh: 濙以故在外最久，至十四年乃還。
units.en: Because of this mission Hu Ying was away longer than any other envoy and did not return until the fourteenth year.
units.literal: Ying because of this mission was abroad longer than anyone else, and only in the fourteenth year did he return.

units.zh: 所至，亦間以民隱聞。
units.en: Along the way he also reported local grievances when he encountered them.
units.literal: Wherever he went, he would from time to time report on the people's hardships.

units.zh: 母喪乞歸，不許，擢禮部左侍郎。
units.en: When his mother died he asked to go into mourning but was refused, and was promoted to left vice minister of rites.
units.literal: His mother died and he begged leave to mourn, but was not permitted; he was promoted Left Vice Minister of Rites.

units.zh: 十七年復出巡江浙、湖、湘諸府。
units.en: In the seventeenth year he was sent out again to inspect Jiangzhe and the lakes-and-rivers region.
units.literal: In the seventeenth year he was again sent on inspection tour through Jiangzhe and the Hu-Xiang prefectures.

units.zh: 二十一年還朝，馳謁帝於宣府。
units.en: In the twenty-first year he came back to court and hurried to see the emperor at Xuanfu.
units.literal: In the twenty-first year he returned to court and galloped to audience with the emperor at Xuanfu.

units.zh: 帝已就寢，聞濙至，急起召入。
units.en: The emperor was already asleep; learning that Hu Ying had come, he rose at once and called him in.
units.literal: The emperor had already retired to bed; hearing that Ying had arrived, he hastily rose and summoned him in.

units.zh: 濙悉以所聞對，漏下四鼓乃出。
units.en: Hu Ying told him everything he had learned, and did not leave until the fourth watch.
units.literal: Ying reported everything he had heard; it was the fourth watch before he emerged.

units.zh: 先濙未至，傳言建文帝蹈海去，帝分遣內臣鄭和數輩浮海下西洋，至是疑始釋。
units.en: Before Hu Ying returned, rumor said the Jianwen emperor had fled overseas, and the emperor had sent eunuchs including Zheng He on voyages to the Western Ocean; only now did his suspicions ease.
units.literal: Before Ying's return, rumor had it that the Jianwen emperor had gone to sea; the emperor had repeatedly sent eunuchs such as Zheng He on voyages to the Western Ocean — at this point his doubts were finally dispelled.

units.zh: 皇太子監國南京，漢王為飛語謗太子。
units.en: While the crown prince governed at Nanjing, the Prince of Han spread rumors to blacken him.
units.literal: When the heir apparent supervised the state in Nanjing, the Prince of Han spread slanders against the crown prince.

units.zh: 帝改濙官南京，因命廉之。
units.en: The emperor transferred Hu Ying to Nanjing and charged him to look into the matter.
units.literal: The emperor changed Ying's post to Nanjing and thereby ordered him to investigate.

units.zh: 濙至，密疏馳上監國七事，言誠敬孝謹無他，帝悅。
units.en: Hu Ying reached Nanjing and sent in a sealed memorial on seven points of the regency, declaring that the heir was reverent, filial, and diligent with no fault found; the emperor was pleased.
units.literal: Ying, on arriving, submitted a secret memorial by express relay on seven points concerning the regency, stating that the prince was sincere, reverent, filial, and careful, with nothing else against him; the emperor was pleased.

units.zh: 仁宗即位，召為行在禮部侍郎，濙陳十事，力言建都北京非便，請還南都，省南北轉運供億之煩。
units.en: When Renzong succeeded, Hu Ying was summoned as vice minister of rites at the traveling court; he presented ten proposals, arguing forcefully that establishing Beijing as the capital was inexpedient, urging a return to Nanjing to spare the burden of north-south transport and supply.
units.literal: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, Ying was summoned as Vice Minister of Rites at the traveling court; Ying presented ten proposals, strongly arguing that making Beijing the capital was inexpedient, asking to return the capital to Nanjing and spare the trouble of north-south transport and supply.

units.zh: 帝皆嘉納。
units.en: The emperor approved them all.
units.literal: The emperor approved them all.

units.zh: 既聞其嘗有密疏，疑之，不果召。
units.en: But learning that he had once sent in a secret memorial, the emperor grew suspicious and did not summon him in the end.
units.literal: But hearing that he had once submitted a secret memorial, the emperor grew suspicious and did not summon him after all.

units.zh: 轉太子賓客，兼南京國子祭酒。
units.en: He was transferred to mentor of the heir apparent while also serving as chancellor of the Nanjing Directorate of Education.
units.literal: He was transferred to be Mentor of the Heir Apparent, concurrently Chancellor of the Nanjing Directorate of Education.

units.zh: 宣宗即位，仍遷禮部左侍郎。
units.en: When Xuande succeeded, Hu Ying was again made left vice minister of rites.
units.literal: When the Xuande emperor took the throne, Ying was again made Left Vice Minister of Rites.

units.zh: 明年來朝，乃留行在禮部，尋進尚書。
units.en: The next year he came to court and was kept at the traveling-court Ministry of Rites, soon advanced to minister.
units.literal: The next year when he came to court he remained at the Nanjing Ministry of Rites and soon was promoted Minister.

units.zh: 漢王反，與楊榮等贊親征。
units.en: When the Prince of Han rebelled, he joined Yang Rong and others in urging the emperor to take the field in person.
units.literal: When the Prince of Han rebelled, he joined Yang Rong and others in urging a personal campaign.

units.zh: 事平，賚予甚厚。
units.en: After the rebellion was put down, his rewards were lavish.
units.literal: After the affair was settled, rewards were very generous.

units.zh: 明年賜第長安右門外，給閽者二人，賜銀章四。
units.en: The following year he received a house outside the Right Chang'an Gate, two gatekeepers, and four silver seals of authority.
units.literal: The next year he was granted a residence outside the Right Chang'an Gate, given two gatekeepers, and awarded four silver seals of authority.

units.zh: 生辰，賜宴其第。
units.en: On his birthday the emperor feasted him at his own house.
units.literal: On his birthday the emperor gave a banquet at his residence.

units.zh: 四年命兼理詹事府事。
units.en: In the fourth Xuande year he was ordered to take charge of the heir apparent's household as well.
units.literal: In the fourth year he was ordered also to administer the Household of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 六年，張本卒，又兼領行在戶部。
units.en: In the sixth year, after Zhang Ben died, he also headed the Nanjing ministry of revenue.
units.literal: In the sixth year, when Zhang Ben died, he also took charge of the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue.

units.zh: 時國用漸廣，濙慮度支不足，蠲租詔下，輒沮格。
units.en: State spending was rising, and Hu Ying, fearing the treasury would not keep pace, often blocked tax-remission edicts.
units.literal: At that time state expenditure was gradually increasing; Ying feared the treasury could not meet it, and whenever an edict remitting taxes came down, he would obstruct it.

units.zh: 帝嘗切戒之，然眷遇不少替。
units.en: The emperor sometimes sharply warned him, but did not withdraw his favor.
units.literal: The emperor sometimes sternly admonished him, yet his favor was little diminished.

units.zh: 嘗曲宴濙及楊士奇、夏原吉、蹇義，曰：「海內無虞，卿等四人力也。」
units.en: He once entertained Hu Ying, Yang Shiqi, Xia Yuanji, and Jian Yi privately and said, "The empire is at peace — the four of you have done this."
units.literal: He once gave a private banquet to Ying, Yang Shiqi, Xia Yuanji, and Jian Yi, saying: "The realm is untroubled — you four have made it so."

units.zh: 英宗即位，詔節冗費。
units.en: When Yingzong came to the throne, an edict called for cutting wasteful spending.
units.literal: When Emperor Yingzong took the throne, an edict ordered curtailment of unnecessary expenses.

units.zh: 濙因奏減上供物，及汰法王以下番僧四五百人，浮費大省。
units.en: Hu Ying proposed reducing court tribute goods and dismissing four or five hundred Tibetan monks below the rank of dharma king, which greatly cut waste.
units.literal: Ying memorialized to reduce tribute items for the court and to dismiss four or five hundred Tibetan monks below the rank of Dharma king, greatly reducing superfluous costs.

units.zh: 正統五年，山西災，詔行寬恤，既而有采買物料之命。
units.en: In Zhengtong five Shanxi suffered disaster and an edict promised relief, but soon after came orders to procure materials on commission.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengtong, Shanxi suffered disaster and an edict ordered relief, but soon afterward came an order for procuring materials on commission.

units.zh: 濙上疏言詔旨宜信。
units.en: Hu Ying memorialized that imperial words should be kept.
units.literal: Ying memorialized that edicts ought to be believed.

units.zh: 又言軍旗營求差遣，因而擾民，宜罷之。
units.en: He also urged an end to camp soldiers' seeking assignment as envoys, which harassed the people.
units.literal: He also said that military households in the camps sought commissions as envoys and in doing so harassed the people, and that this should be stopped.

units.zh: 皆報可。
units.en: Both suggestions were accepted.
units.literal: Both proposals were approved.

units.zh: 行在禮部印失，詔弗問，命改鑄。
units.en: When the seal of the Nanjing ministry of rites was lost, the emperor forbade investigation and ordered a new seal cast.
units.literal: The seal of the Nanjing Ministry of Rites was lost; the emperor ordered that no inquiry be made and a new seal cast.

units.zh: 已，又失，被劾下獄。
units.en: Soon it was lost again; he was impeached and put in prison.
units.literal: Before long it was lost again and he was impeached and imprisoned.

units.zh: 未幾，印獲，復職。
units.en: Not long after, the seal turned up and he was reinstated.
units.literal: Before long the seal was recovered and he was restored to office.

units.zh: 九年，年七十，乞致仕，不許。
units.en: In the ninth year, at seventy, he asked to retire but was refused.
units.literal: In the ninth year, at age seventy, he asked to retire, but was not permitted.

units.zh: 英宗北狩，群臣聚哭於朝，有議南遷者。
units.en: When Yingzong was captured in the north, ministers wept together at court, and some urged moving the capital south.
units.literal: When Emperor Yingzong was taken north at the Tumu disaster, the ministers gathered weeping at court and some spoke of moving the capital south.

units.zh: 濙曰：「文皇定陵寢於此，示子孫以不拔之計也。」
units.en: Hu Ying said, "Emperor Wen laid the imperial tombs here to show his line a capital they must not abandon."
units.literal: Ying said: "Emperor Wen set the imperial tombs here, showing his descendants a plan that would not be uprooted."

units.zh: 與侍郎于謙合，中外始有固誌。
units.en: Together with Vice Minister Yu Qian he stiffened resolve inside and outside the court.
units.literal: He and Vice Minister Yu Qian united in this, and only then did court and country settle on holding firm.

units.zh: 景帝即位，進太子太傅。
units.en: When the Jingtai emperor succeeded, Hu Ying was made grand tutor to the heir apparent.
units.literal: When Emperor Jingdai took the throne, Ying was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 楊善使也先，濙言上皇蒙塵久，宜附進服食，不報。
units.en: When Yang Shan went on embassy to the Oirats, Hu Ying urged that supplies be sent to the captive emperor, who had long suffered in the north, but the court did not reply.
units.literal: When Yang Shan was sent to the Oirats, Ying urged that because the retired emperor had long been in hardship, food and clothing should be sent along with the mission, but there was no response.

units.zh: 上皇將還，命禮部具奉迎儀。
units.en: As the retired emperor was about to return, the throne ordered the ministry of rites to draw up welcome rites.
units.literal: When the retired emperor was about to return, the emperor ordered the Ministry of Rites to prepare the welcome ceremony.

units.zh: 濙等議遣禮部署迎於龍虎臺，錦衣具法駕迎居庸關，百司迎土城外，諸將迎教場門；
units.en: Hu Ying and his colleagues proposed that rites officials meet him at Longhu Terrace, the imperial guard deploy the state carriage at Juyong Pass, all ministries receive him outside the earthen city wall, and generals receive him at the drill ground;
units.literal: Ying and the others proposed that the Ministry of Rites send officials to welcome him at Longhu Terrace, the Brocade-Imperial Guard provide the imperial carriage to welcome him at Juyong Pass, the hundred officials welcome him outside the earth wall of the city, and the generals welcome him at the drill-ground gate;

units.zh: 上皇自安定門入，進東安門，於東上北門南面坐；
units.en: the retired emperor would enter by the Anding Gate, go on to the Dong'an Gate, and take a seat facing south at the upper north gate on the east side;
units.literal: the retired emperor would enter by the Anding Gate, proceed to the Dong'an Gate, and be seated facing south at the north gate on the eastern upper level;

units.zh: 皇帝謁見畢，百官朝見，上皇入南城大內。
units.en: after the reigning emperor had performed his visit, the officials would attend, and the retired emperor would enter the inner quarters of the Southern Palace.
units.literal: after the emperor paid his respects, the hundred officials would have audience, and the retired emperor would enter the Great Inner Palace of the Southern City.

units.zh: 議上，傳旨以一轎二馬迎於居庸關，至安定門易法駕，余如奏。
units.en: The proposal went up; the response was that a single sedan and two horses should meet him at Juyong Pass, the full imperial carriage only at the Anding Gate, with the rest as proposed.
units.literal: When the proposal went up, an order was transmitted that one sedan chair and two horses should welcome him at Juyong Pass, and at the Anding Gate the state carriage should be exchanged for — the rest as memorialized.

units.zh: 給事中劉福等言禮太薄。
units.en: Supervising secretary Liu Fu and others protested that the ceremony was too mean.
units.literal: Supervising Secretary Liu Fu and others said the rites were too meager.

units.zh: 帝報曰：「朕尊大兄為太上皇帝，尊禮無加矣。
units.en: The emperor answered, "I honor my elder brother as Retired Emperor; no welcome could exceed that.
units.literal: The emperor replied: I honor my elder brother as Retired Emperor; no honor can be added.

units.zh: 福等顧雲太薄，其意何居？
units.en: Why do Liu Fu and his fellows call the rites too thin — what are they driving at?
units.literal: Why do Fu and the others speak of the rites being too meager — what is their intent?

units.zh: 禮部其會官詳察之。」
units.en: Let the ministry of rites convene officials and review this carefully."
units.literal: Let the Ministry of Rites assemble officials and examine this in detail.

units.zh: 濙等言：「諸臣意無他，欲陛下篤親親耳。」
units.en: Hu Ying and his colleagues replied, "Their only aim is that Your Majesty should show deep family feeling."
units.literal: Ying and the others said: "The ministers have no other intent; they wish Your Majesty to deepen the bonds of kinship."

units.zh: 帝曰：「昨得太上皇書，具言迎駕之禮宜從簡損，朕豈得違之。」
units.en: The emperor said, "Yesterday I received a letter from the Retired Emperor stating plainly that the welcome should be kept simple; how could I go against it?"
units.literal: The emperor said: "Yesterday I received a letter from the Retired Emperor, stating in full that the welcome rites should be kept simple and reduced — how can I disobey?"

units.zh: 群臣乃不敢言。
units.en: The officials fell silent.
units.literal: The ministers then dared not speak further.

units.zh: 會千戶龔遂榮為書投大學士高谷，言奉迎宜厚，具言唐肅宗迎上皇故事。
units.en: Meanwhile the qianhu Gong Suirong sent Grand Secretary Gao Gu a letter arguing that the welcome should be lavish and citing Tang Suzong's reception of his father.
units.literal: Meanwhile Qianhu Gong Suirong wrote a letter and sent it to Grand Secretary Gao Gu, saying the welcome ought to be generous and citing in full the Tang precedent of Emperor Suzong welcoming the retired emperor.

units.zh: 谷袖之以朝，與王直等共觀之。
units.en: Gao Gu carried it to court and read it with Wang Zhi and the others.
units.literal: Gu tucked it in his sleeve and took it to court, and with Wang Zhi and the others examined it together.

units.zh: 直與濙欲聞之帝，為都御史王文所阻，而給事中葉盛竟以聞。
units.en: Wang Zhi and Hu Ying wanted to report it to the throne but were stopped by Censor-in-Chief Wang Wen; supervising secretary Ye Sheng nevertheless brought it forward.
units.literal: Zhi and Ying wished to inform the emperor, but were blocked by Censor-in-Chief Wang Wen; yet Supervising Secretary Ye Sheng in the end reported it.

units.zh: 盛同官林聰復劾直、濙、谷等，皆股肱大臣，有聞必告，不宜偶語竊議。
units.en: Ye's colleague Lin Cong impeached Wang Zhi, Hu Ying, Gao Gu, and the rest for talking in private instead of reporting what they knew, as pillar ministers should.
units.literal: Ye's colleague Lin Cong again impeached Zhi, Ying, Gu, and the rest, saying that as pillar ministers, whatever they learned they ought to report, and ought not to whisper in private deliberation.

units.zh: 有詔索書。
units.en: An edict was issued demanding the letter.
units.literal: An imperial order was issued to demand the letter.

units.zh: 濙等因以書進，且言：「肅宗迎上皇典禮，今日正可仿行。
units.en: Hu Ying and his colleagues then submitted the letter and added, "The rites with which Tang Suzong welcomed his father are just what should be followed now.
units.literal: Ying and the others thereupon submitted the letter, and moreover said: "The ceremony by which Emperor Suzong welcomed the retired emperor is exactly what should be followed today.

units.zh: 陛下宜躬迎安定門外，分遣大臣迎龍虎臺。」
units.en: Your Majesty should meet him in person outside the Anding Gate and send senior ministers to Longhu Terrace."
units.literal: Your Majesty ought personally to welcome him outside the Anding Gate and dispatch great ministers to welcome him at Longhu Terrace."

units.zh: 帝不悅曰：「第從朕命，無事紛更。」
units.en: The emperor, angered, said, "Do as I command; do not keep stirring this up."
units.literal: The emperor, displeased, said: "Just follow my command; do not stir up trouble."

units.zh: 上皇至，居南城宮。
units.en: When the Retired Emperor returned, he lived in the palace of the Southern City.
units.literal: When the Retired Emperor arrived, he dwelt in the Southern City palace.

units.zh: 濙請帝明年正旦率群臣朝延安門，不許。
units.en: Hu Ying asked that on the next New Year's Day the emperor lead the ministers in homage at the Yan'an Gate, but the request was denied.
units.literal: Ying asked that on New Year's Day of the following year the emperor lead the ministers in audience at the Yan'an Gate, but permission was refused.

units.zh: 上皇萬壽節，請令百官拜賀延安門，亦不許。
units.en: On the Retired Emperor's birthday Hu Ying again asked that officials offer congratulations at the Yan'an Gate; again the request was denied.
units.literal: On the Retired Emperor's longevity birthday, Ying again asked that the hundred officials offer congratulations at the Yan'an Gate; again permission was refused.

units.zh: 三年正月與王直並進少傅。
units.en: In the third year, first month, he and Wang Zhi were both promoted to junior grand tutor.
units.literal: In the first month of the third year he and Wang Zhi were both advanced to Junior Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 易太子，加兼太子太師。
units.en: When the heir was changed he was also made grand preceptor to the crown prince.
units.literal: When the crown prince was replaced, he was additionally made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 王文惡林聰，文致其罪，欲殺之。
units.en: Wang Wen hated Lin Cong, fabricated charges against him, and sought his death.
units.literal: Wang Wen hated Lin Cong; he forged charges against him and wished to kill him.

units.zh: 濙不肯署，遂稱疾，數日不朝。
units.en: Hu Ying refused to countersign, then pleaded illness and stayed away from court for days.
units.literal: Ying refused to sign, then claimed illness and for several days did not attend court.

units.zh: 帝使興安問疾。
units.en: The emperor sent the eunuch Xing An to ask after his health.
units.literal: The emperor sent Xing An to inquire after his illness.

units.zh: 對曰：「老臣本無疾，聞欲殺林聰，殊驚悸耳。」
units.en: He answered, "This old minister is not ill; hearing they meant to kill Lin Cong, I was only shaken with alarm."
units.literal: He replied: "This old minister has no illness; hearing that they wished to kill Lin Cong, I was greatly startled and distressed."

units.zh: 聰由是得釋。
units.en: Lin Cong was released as a result.
units.literal: Lin Cong was thereby released.

units.zh: 英宗復位，力疾入朝，遂求去。
units.en: When Yingzong was restored Hu Ying dragged himself to court despite illness, then asked to retire.
units.literal: When Emperor Yingzong was restored, Ying forced himself to attend court despite illness, then asked to leave office.

units.zh: 賜璽書、白金、楮幣、襲衣，給驛，官其一子錦衣，世鎮撫。
units.en: He received a sealed letter, white gold, paper money, and court robes, an imperial courier, and one son was made a hereditary garrison commander in the imperial guard.
units.literal: He was granted a sealed letter, white gold, paper currency, and ceremonial robes, given an express post, and one son was made an officer in the Brocade-Imperial Guard as hereditary garrison commander.

units.zh: 濙歷事六朝，垂六十年，中外稱耆德。
units.en: Hu Ying had served six reigns for nearly sixty years and was called a venerable elder at court and beyond.
units.literal: Ying had served through six reigns, nearly sixty years, and was praised inside and outside the court as a venerable worthy.

units.zh: 及歸，有三弟，年皆七十余，須眉皓白，燕聚一堂，因名之曰「壽愷」。
units.en: After retiring he had three younger brothers, all past seventy, white of brow and beard, feasting together in one hall he named the "Hall of Longevity and Joy".
units.literal: On returning home he had three younger brothers, all over seventy, with eyebrows and beards snow-white, feasting together in one hall — he named it the "Hall of Longevity and Harmony".

units.zh: 又七年始卒，年八十九。
units.en: Seven years later he died, aged eighty-nine.
units.literal: Seven years more passed before he died, aged eighty-nine.

units.zh: 贈太保，謚忠安。
units.en: He was posthumously made grand guardian with the posthumous title Zhong'an.
units.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian with the posthumous name Zhong'an.

units.zh: 濙節儉寬厚，喜怒不形於色，能以身下人。
units.en: Hu Ying was frugal, generous, and even-tempered; he could set himself below others.
units.literal: Ying was frugal, generous, and mild; joy and anger did not show on his face, and he could humble himself before others.

units.zh: 在禮部久，表賀祥瑞，以官當首署名，人因謂其性善承迎。
units.en: Long at the ministry of rites, he signed first on memorials of congratulation for auspicious omens, and people said he was eager to please.
units.literal: Long in the Ministry of Rites, when memorializing congratulations on auspicious omens he would sign first as the ranking official, and people therefore said he had a disposition inclined to flattery.

units.zh: 南城人龔謙多妖術，濙薦為天文生，又薦道士仰彌高曉陰陽兵法，使守邊，時頗譏之。
units.en: Gong Qian of the Southern City practiced many occult arts; Hu Ying recommended him as an astronomical student and recommended the Daoist Yang Migao, versed in yin-yang and warfare, to guard the frontier — acts widely mocked at the time.
units.literal: Gong Qian of the Southern City had many occult arts; Ying recommended him as an astronomical student, and also recommended the Daoist Yang Migao, skilled in yin-yang and military strategy, to guard the frontier — at the time he was much ridiculed.

units.zh: 王直，字行儉，泰和人。
units.en: Wang Zhi, courtesy name Xingqian, was from Taihe.
units.literal: Wang Zhi, styled Xingqian, was a native of Taihe.

units.zh: 父伯貞，洪武十五年以明經聘至京。
units.en: His father Wang Bo Zhen was summoned to the capital in Hongwu fifteen through the classics recruitment.
units.literal: His father Bo Zhen, in the fifteenth year of Hongwu, was summoned to the capital through the classics-examination recruitment.

units.zh: 時應詔者五百余人，伯貞對第一。
units.en: More than five hundred men answered the summons; Bo Zhen ranked first.
units.literal: At that time more than five hundred men answered the imperial summons; Bo Zhen ranked first in the examination.

units.zh: 授試僉事，分巡廣東雷州。
units.en: He was made probationary associate administrator and sent to inspect Leizhou in Guangdong.
units.literal: He was appointed probationary associate administrator and sent on circuit inspection of Leizhou in Guangdong.

units.zh: 復呂塘廢渠，清鹽法。
units.en: He restored the abandoned Lütang canal and reformed the salt laws.
units.literal: He restored the abandoned channel at Lütang and cleared up the salt regulations.

units.zh: 會罷分巡官，召還為戶部主事。
units.en: When circuit inspectors were abolished he was recalled and made a principal secretary in the ministry of revenue.
units.literal: When circuit inspectors were abolished, he was recalled and made a principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

units.zh: 以父喪服闋，不時起，謫居安慶。
units.en: After his father's mourning he failed to resume office on time and was banished to Anqing.
units.literal: After his mourning period for his father ended, he did not return to office promptly and was banished to live at Anqing.

units.zh: 建文初，復以薦知瓊州，崖州黎相仇殺，以反聞，且用兵。
units.en: Early in Jianwen he was recommended again and made prefect of Qiongzhou; Li clans on Yazhou's cliffs feuded and killed one another, the affair was reported as rebellion, and troops were to be sent.
units.literal: At the beginning of Jianwen he was again recommended and appointed prefect of Qiongzhou; the Li of Yazhou on the cliffs feuded and killed one another, which was reported as rebellion, and troops were about to be used.

units.zh: 伯貞捕其首惡，兵遂罷。
units.en: Bo Zhen seized the ringleaders and the campaign was called off.
units.literal: Bo Zhen arrested the ringleaders and the troops were then halted.

units.zh: 瓊田歲常三獲，以賦軍，軍不時受，俟民乏，乃急斂以要利。
units.en: Qiong fields often yielded three crops a year, taxed to supply the army; the army delayed collection until the people were desperate, then squeezed them for profit.
units.literal: Fields in Qiong normally yielded three harvests a year, the produce assigned to supply the army; the army did not accept it on schedule but waited until the people were short, then pressed collection to profit.

units.zh: 伯貞為立期，三輸之，弊始絕。
units.en: Bo Zhen fixed three delivery dates, and the abuse ended.
units.literal: Bo Zhen established fixed periods for three deliveries, and the abuse was ended.

units.zh: 居數年，大治，流民占籍者萬余。
units.en: Within a few years the prefecture was well governed and more than ten thousand vagrants were registered.
units.literal: After several years there was great good order, and more than ten thousand vagrant people were registered on the rolls.

units.zh: 憂歸，卒於家。
units.en: He went home in mourning and died there.
units.literal: He returned home in grief and died at home.

units.zh: 直幼而端重，家貧力學。
units.en: Wang Zhi was grave and steady from childhood; though poor he studied hard.
units.literal: Zhi from youth was dignified and steady, and though his family was poor he studied diligently.

units.zh: 舉永樂二年進士，改庶吉士，與曾棨、王英等二十八人同讀書文淵閣。
units.en: In Yongle two he passed the metropolitan examination, became a Hanlin bachelor, and with Zeng Qi, Wang Ying, and twenty-eight others studied in the Wenyuan Pavilion.
units.literal: In the second year of Yongle he passed the metropolitan examination, was changed to Hanlin bachelor, and with Zeng Qi, Wang Ying, and twenty-eight others together studied in the Wenyuan Pavilion.

units.zh: 帝善其文，召入內閣，俾屬草。
units.en: The emperor admired his writing and summoned him to the Grand Secretariat to draft documents.
units.literal: The emperor admired his writing and summoned him into the Grand Secretariat to draft documents.

units.zh: 尋授修撰。
units.en: Soon he was made a compiler.
units.literal: Soon he was appointed compiler.

units.zh: 歷事仁宗、宣宗，累遷少詹事兼侍讀學士。
units.en: Under Renzong and Xuanzong he rose to junior chamberlain and lecturing academician.
units.literal: Through the reigns of Renzong and Xuanzong he rose repeatedly to Junior Chamberlain concurrently with lecturing academician.

units.zh: 正統三年，《宣宗實錄》成。
units.en: In Zhengtong three the Veritable Records of Xuanzong were completed.
units.literal: In the third year of Zhengtong, the Veritable Records of Xuanzong were completed.

units.zh: 進禮部侍郎，學士如故。
units.en: He was promoted vice minister of rites while keeping his academician post.
units.literal: He was promoted Vice Minister of Rites, retaining his academician post.

units.zh: 五年出蒞部事。
units.en: In the fifth year he took charge of ministry business in person.
units.literal: In the fifth year he went out to take charge of ministry affairs.

units.zh: 尚書胡濙悉以部政付之，直處之若素習者。
units.en: Minister Hu Ying turned all ministry affairs over to him; Wang Zhi handled them as if long practiced.
units.literal: Minister Hu Ying entrusted all ministry business to him, and Zhi handled it as if long practiced.

units.zh: 八年正月代郭琎為吏部尚書。
units.en: In the eighth year, first month, he replaced Guo Jin as minister of personnel.
units.literal: In the first month of the eighth year he replaced Guo Jin as Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 十一年，戶部侍郎奈亨附王振，構郎中趙敏，詞連直及侍郎曹義、趙新，並下獄。
units.en: In the eleventh year revenue vice minister Nai Heng, siding with Wang Zhen, framed director Zhao Min and implicated Wang Zhi and vice ministers Cao Yi and Zhao Xin; all were imprisoned.
units.literal: In the eleventh year, Vice Minister of Revenue Nai Heng, attaching himself to Wang Zhen, fabricated charges against Director Lang Zhao Min, implicating Zhi and Vice Ministers Cao Yi and Zhao Xin, who were all imprisoned.

units.zh: 三法司廷鞫，論亨斬，直等贖徒。
units.en: The three judicial offices tried them in open court: Nai Heng was sentenced to death, Wang Zhi and the others to penal service.
units.literal: The Three Judicial Offices tried them at court; Nai Heng was sentenced to beheading, Zhi and the others to commuting service.

units.zh: 帝宥直、義，奪亨、新俸。
units.en: The emperor pardoned Wang Zhi and Cao Yi and docked the salaries of Nai Heng and Zhao Xin.
units.literal: The emperor pardoned Zhi and Yi, and confiscated Nai Heng's and Xin's salaries.

units.zh: 帝將親征也先，直率廷臣力諫曰：「國家備邊最為謹嚴。
units.en: When the emperor was about to take the field against Esen personally, Wang Zhi led the ministers in strong remonstrance: "The empire guards its frontiers with the utmost care.
units.literal: When the emperor was about to campaign personally against Esen, Zhi led the court ministers in forceful remonstrance: "The state's frontier defense is maintained with greatest strictness.

units.zh: 謀臣猛將，堅甲利兵，隨處充滿，且耕且守，是以久安。
units.en: Counsellors and bold generals, stout armor and sharp weapons, fill every post; men farm and guard together, and so the realm has long been at peace.
units.literal: Counsellors and fierce generals, strong armor and sharp weapons, are plentiful everywhere, farming and guarding together — thus long peace is secured.

units.zh: 今敵肆猖獗，違天悖理，陛下但宜固封疆，申號令，堅壁清野，蓄銳以待之，可圖必勝。
units.en: Now the enemy rampages in defiance of Heaven and right; Your Majesty need only hold the borders firm, issue orders, clear the countryside, and gather strength to wait — victory can be assured.
units.literal: Now the enemy runs riot in defiance of Heaven and reason; Your Majesty need only secure the borders, issue commands, clear the countryside and hold fast, and store sharpness to await them — victory can be planned for.

units.zh: 不必親禦六師，遠臨塞下。
units.en: There is no need for Your Majesty to lead the Six Armies in person to the distant frontier.
units.literal: There is no need for Your Majesty personally to lead the Six Armies far to the borderlands.

units.zh: 況秋署未退，旱氣未回，青草不豐，水泉猶塞，士馬之用未充。
units.en: Moreover autumn heat lingers, drought has not lifted, grass is thin, springs are low, and men and horses are not ready.
units.literal: Moreover the autumn heat has not yet passed, drought has not yet broken, green pasture is not rich, springs are still blocked, and horses and men are not fully supplied.

units.zh: 兵兇戰危，臣等以為不可。」
units.en: War is perilous — we your ministers believe it must not be done."
units.literal: War is perilous — we your subjects believe it cannot be done."

units.zh: 帝不從，命直留守。
units.en: The emperor would not listen and ordered Wang Zhi to remain and guard the capital.
units.literal: The emperor did not assent and ordered Zhi to remain on guard.

units.zh: 王師覆於土木。
units.en: The imperial army was destroyed at Tumu.
units.literal: The imperial army was destroyed at Tumu.

units.zh: 大臣群請太后立皇子為皇太子，命郕王攝政。
units.en: The great ministers asked the empress dowager to install the prince as heir apparent and have the Prince of Cheng act as regent.
units.literal: The great ministers together asked the Empress Dowager to establish the prince as heir apparent and order the Prince of Cheng to govern as regent.

units.zh: 已，勸王即位，以安反側。
units.en: Soon they urged the prince to ascend the throne to steady the realm.
units.literal: Before long they urged the prince to take the throne to secure the realm against unrest.

units.zh: 時變起倉卒，朝臣議屢上，皆直為首。
units.en: In the sudden crisis memorials poured in, and Wang Zhi led them all.
units.literal: At that time sudden turmoil arose and court debates came up repeatedly — Zhi led them all.

units.zh: 而直自以不如于謙，每事推下之，雍容鎮率而已。
units.en: Yet Wang Zhi felt himself inferior to Yu Qian and always deferred to him, himself remaining calm and steady.
units.literal: Yet Zhi himself felt he was not the equal of Yu Qian and always deferred to him in affairs, remaining calm and steady in command.

units.zh: 加太子太保。
units.en: He was made grand guardian of the heir apparent.
units.literal: He was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 景泰元年，也先使使議和，且請還上皇，下禮部議未決。
units.en: In Jingtai one Esen sent envoys to discuss peace and ask for the retired emperor's return; the ministry of rites debated without decision.
units.literal: In the first year of Jingtai, Esen sent envoys to discuss peace and also asked return of the retired emperor; the Ministry of Rites deliberated but no decision was reached.

units.zh: 直率群臣上言曰：「太上皇惑細人言，輕身一出，至於蒙塵。
units.en: Wang Zhi led the ministers in memorializing: "The Retired Emperor was misled by petty men and went forth rashly, until he fell into hardship.
units.literal: Zhi led the ministers in memorializing: "The Retired Emperor was misled by petty men's words and rashly went forth once, until he suffered in exile.

units.zh: 陛下宵衣旰食，征天下兵，與群臣兆姓同心僇力，期滅此朝食，以雪不共戴天之恥。
units.en: Your Majesty rises early and retires late, raises armies from all the realm, and with ministers and people alike strives to destroy the foe at one stroke and wash away a shame that cannot be borne.
units.literal: Your Majesty rises early and retires late, raising troops from all the realm, and with ministers and the myriad people together exerting strength, resolved to destroy them at breakfast and wash away the shame we cannot share Heaven with them.

units.zh: 乃者天誘其衷，也先有悔心之萌，而來求成於我，請還乘輿，此轉禍為福之機也。
units.en: Now Heaven has moved their hearts: Esen shows repentance and seeks peace, asking to return the imperial carriage — a chance to turn disaster into blessing.
units.literal: Now Heaven has guided their hearts — Esen has a stir of repentance and comes seeking peace with us, asking return of the imperial carriage; this is a chance to turn misfortune to blessing.

units.zh: 望陛下俯從其請，遣使往報，因察其誠偽而撫納之，奉太上皇以歸，少慰祖宗之心。
units.en: We beg Your Majesty to accept, send envoys to answer, test their sincerity, and bring the Retired Emperor home to comfort our ancestors' spirits.
units.literal: We hope Your Majesty will humbly accept their request, send envoys to reply, observe their sincerity and receive them, and bring the Retired Emperor home, somewhat comforting the hearts of our ancestors.

units.zh: 陛下天位已定，太上皇還，不復蒞天下事。
units.en: Your Majesty's throne is secure; when the Retired Emperor returns he will not rule again.
units.literal: Your Majesty's throne is already settled; when the Retired Emperor returns he will not again administer the realm.

units.zh: 陛下第崇奉之，則天倫厚而天眷益隆，誠古今盛事也。」
units.en: Honor him richly and family bonds deepen and Heaven's favor grows — a wonder of all ages."
units.literal: If Your Majesty only honors him with respect, then human bonds are deep and Heaven's favor grows — truly a great event of past and present."

units.zh: 帝曰：「卿等言良然。
units.en: The emperor said, "What you say is sound.
units.literal: The emperor said: "What you say is indeed so.

units.zh: 但前後使者五輩往，終不得要領。
units.en: But five missions have already gone without clear result.
units.literal: But envoys have gone five times before without any clear result.

units.zh: 今復遣使，設彼假送駕為名，來犯京師，豈不為蒼生患。
units.en: If we send again and they use escorting the emperor as a pretext to strike the capital, will the people not suffer?
units.literal: If we send envoys again and they falsely use escorting the imperial carriage as a pretext to strike at the capital, will that not be calamity for the people?

units.zh: 賊詐難信，其更議之。」
units.en: The enemy is treacherous — debate this further."
units.literal: The bandits are deceitful and hard to trust — deliberate further."

units.zh: 已而瓦剌別部阿剌使復至，胡濙等復以為言。
units.en: Soon envoys of the Oirat branch under Ala arrived, and Hu Ying and others urged the same again.
units.literal: Before long envoys of the Oirat sub-branch under Alag arrived, and Hu Ying and others again urged the same.

units.zh: 於是帝御文華殿門，召諸大臣及言官諭以宜絕狀。
units.en: The emperor then held court at the Wenhua Hall gate, summoned ministers and censors, and told them to reject the overture.
units.literal: Thereupon the emperor held court at the Wenhua Hall gate, summoned the great ministers and remonstrance officials, and instructed them on how to reject their petition.

units.zh: 直對曰：「必遣使，毋貽後悔。」
units.en: Wang Zhi answered, "We must send envoys — do not leave regret behind."
units.literal: Zhi replied: "Envoys must be sent — do not leave regret behind."

units.zh: 帝不悅。
units.en: The emperor was displeased.
units.literal: The emperor was displeased.

units.zh: 于謙前為解，帝意釋。
units.en: Yu Qian stepped forward to explain, and the emperor's anger eased.
units.literal: Yu Qian came forward to explain, and the emperor's mind eased.

units.zh: 群臣既退，太監興安匍匐出呼曰：「若等固欲遣使，有文天祥、富弼其人乎？」
units.en: After the ministers withdrew the eunuch Xing An crawled out calling, "If you insist on envoys, are there men like Wen Tianxiang or Fu Bi among you?"
units.literal: After the ministers withdrew, the eunuch Xing An crawled out calling: "If you insist on sending envoys, are there men like Wen Tianxiang or Fu Bi among you?"

units.zh: 直大言曰：「廷臣惟天子使，既食其祿，敢辭難乎！」
units.en: Wang Zhi said loudly, "Court ministers serve at the emperor's command; having eaten the state's grain, how dare we refuse hardship!"
units.literal: Zhi said loudly: "Court ministers are the emperor's to dispatch; having eaten his salary, how dare we shrink from difficulty!"

units.zh: 言之再，聲色愈厲。
units.en: He said it twice, his voice growing fiercer.
units.literal: He said it twice, his voice and manner growing fiercer.

units.zh: 安語塞，乃議遣使，命李實、羅綺往。
units.en: Xing An was silenced; they then agreed to send envoys and appointed Li Shi and Luo Qi.
units.literal: An was silenced; they then deliberated on sending envoys and ordered Li Shi and Luo Qi to go.

units.zh: 既行，而瓦剌可汗脫脫不花及也先使先後至，將遣歸。
units.en: After they had gone, the Oirat khan Totoq Buqa and Esen's envoys arrived in succession, ready to send the emperor back.
units.literal: After they had departed, the Oirat khan Totoq Buqa and Esen's envoys arrived one after another, intending to send the emperor back.

units.zh: 使者謂館伴曰：「中國關外十四城皆為我有。
units.en: The envoys told the escorts, "Fourteen cities beyond the pass are already ours.
units.literal: The envoys said to the escorting officials: "Fourteen cities outside the passes are all ours.

units.zh: 前阿剌知院使來，尚遣人偕往。
units.en: When the former Ala zhiguan envoy came, your court still sent men with him.
units.literal: When the former Alag zhiguan envoy came, men were still sent to accompany him.

units.zh: 今亦必得大臣同行，庶有濟。」
units.en: Now you must send a senior minister with us, or nothing will come of it."
units.literal: Now we must also have a great minister go with us, or there will be no help for it."

units.zh: 胡濙以聞，下廷議。
units.en: Hu Ying reported this and the court debated.
units.literal: Hu Ying reported this, and the court deliberated.

units.zh: 直等固請，乃遣楊善等報之。
units.en: Wang Zhi and others pressed hard, and Yang Shan and others were sent in reply.
units.literal: Zhi and the others strongly urged it, and Yang Shan and others were sent in reply.

units.zh: 比實還，又以也先使至，具言也先欲和狀。
units.en: When Li Shi returned, Esen's envoy had come again, stating Esen's wish for peace in full.
units.literal: By the time Shi returned, Esen's envoy had again arrived, stating in full Esen's wish for peace.

units.zh: 直與寧陽侯陳懋等上疏，請更遣使賫禮幣往迎上皇，不許。
units.en: Wang Zhi with the Marquis of Ningyang Chen Mao and others asked that another envoy go with gifts to welcome the retired emperor — refused.
units.literal: Zhi with the Marquis of Ningyang Chen Mao and others memorialized asking that another envoy be sent bearing gifts to welcome the retired emperor — not permitted.

units.zh: 復上疏曰：「臣等與李實語，具得彼中情事。
units.en: They memorialized again: "We questioned Li Shi and learned the full situation there.
units.literal: They memorialized again: "We spoke with Li Shi and learned fully the situation there.

units.zh: 其所需衣物資斧者，上皇言也；
units.en: The clothing, supplies, and axes they need — the retired emperor spoke of these;
units.literal: The clothing, supplies, and axes they need — the retired emperor spoke of these;

units.zh: 而奉迎車駕，也先意也。
units.en: but escorting the imperial carriage home was Esen's intent.
units.literal: but escorting the imperial carriage back was Esen's intent.

units.zh: 昨者脫脫不花及阿剌知院使來，皆有報使。
units.en: When Totoq Buqa and the Ala zhiguan envoy came, reply envoys were sent both times.
units.literal: Yesterday Totoq Buqa and the Alag zhiguan envoy came, and in both cases reply envoys were sent.

units.zh: 今也先使以迎請為辭，乃不遣使與偕，是疑敵而召兵也。」
units.en: Now Esen's envoy comes to welcome the emperor, yet no envoy goes with him — this doubts the enemy and invites war."
units.literal: Now Esen's envoy comes with welcoming as his plea, yet no envoy is sent with him — this is to doubt the enemy and invite war."

units.zh: 又不許。
units.en: Again refused.
units.literal: Again not permitted.

units.zh: 已而實自言於帝。
units.en: Soon Li Shi himself spoke to the emperor.
units.literal: Before long Shi himself spoke to the emperor.

units.zh: 帝第報也先書，就令楊善迎歸而已。
units.en: The emperor only wrote Esen and ordered Yang Shan to bring the emperor home — nothing more.
units.literal: The emperor merely replied to Esen in writing and ordered Yang Shan to welcome him home — that was all.

units.zh: 直等復上言：「今北使已發，願本上皇之心，順臣民之願，因彼悔心，遣使往報，以圖迎復，此不待計而決者也。
units.en: Wang Zhi and others memorialized again: "Northern envoys have already set out; in accord with the retired emperor's heart and the people's wish, seize their repentance and send envoys to plan his welcome — this needs no debate.
units.literal: Zhi and the others memorialized again: "Northern envoys have already set out; we wish in accord with the retired emperor's heart and the people's wish, following their repentance, to send envoys to report and plan his welcome — this need not be debated.

units.zh: 不然，眾誌難犯，違天不祥，彼將執為兵端，邊事益棘，京師亦不得高枕臥矣。」
units.en: Otherwise public feeling cannot be defied, Heaven is offended, they will use this as a pretext for war, the frontier will worsen, and the capital cannot rest easy."
units.literal: Otherwise popular will is hard to defy, Heaven is angered by defiance, they will seize on this as a pretext for war, frontier affairs will grow worse, and the capital cannot sleep easy either."

units.zh: 帝乃命群臣擇使，直與陳懋等請仍遣實。
units.en: The emperor then ordered ministers to choose envoys; Wang Zhi and Chen Mao asked that Li Shi go again.
units.literal: The emperor then ordered the ministers to choose envoys; Zhi with Chen Mao and others asked that Shi be sent again.

units.zh: 報曰：「候善歸議之。」
units.en: The reply: "Wait until Yang Shan returns, then debate."
units.literal: The reply: "Wait until Shan returns to deliberate."

units.zh: 御史畢鑾等復上疏，力言：「就令彼以詐來，我以誠往，萬一不測，則我之兵力固在。」
units.en: Censor Bi Luan and others memorialized forcefully: "Even if they come in deceit and we go in good faith, if the worst happens our armies remain strong."
units.literal: Censor Bi Luan and others again memorialized, forcefully stating: "Even if they come in deceit and we go in sincerity, if the worst happens our military strength remains firm."

units.zh: 帝終不聽。
units.en: The emperor would not be moved.
units.literal: The emperor in the end would not listen.

units.zh: 已而善竟奉上皇還。
units.en: Before long Yang Shan did bring the retired emperor home.
units.literal: Before long Shan in the end brought the retired emperor home.

units.zh: 二年，也先遣使入貢，且請答使。
units.en: In the second year Esen sent envoys with tribute and also asked for return envoys.
units.literal: In the second year Esen sent envoys to offer tribute and also requested return envoys.

units.zh: 直屢疏言：「邊備未修，芻糧未積，瘡痍未復，宜如其請。
units.en: Wang Zhi memorialized repeatedly: "The frontier is not secured, fodder and grain are not stocked, and the realm is not yet healed — we should grant their request.
units.literal: Zhi repeatedly memorialized: "Frontier defenses are not repaired, fodder and grain are not stored up, and the wounds of war are not healed — we should grant their request.

units.zh: 遣使往以觀虛實，開導其善。」
units.en: Send envoys to test their sincerity and lead them toward peace."
units.literal: Send envoys to observe their true state and guide them toward what is good."

units.zh: 不許。
units.en: The request was refused.
units.literal: Permission was refused.

units.zh: 無何，也先遣騎入塞，以報使為辭。
units.en: Soon Esen sent cavalry across the border on the pretext of escorting return envoys.
units.literal: Before long Esen sent horsemen into the borderlands, using reply envoys as their pretext.

units.zh: 直與群臣復請之，卒不許。
units.en: Wang Zhi and the ministers asked again; in the end the court still refused.
units.literal: Zhi and the ministers again requested it; in the end permission was refused.

units.zh: 直等乃上疏言：「陛下銳意治兵，為戰守計，真大有為之主。
units.en: Wang Zhi and others then memorialized: "Your Majesty is resolved to train the army and plan for attack and defense — truly a ruler of great purpose.
units.literal: Zhi and the others thereupon memorialized: "Your Majesty is keen to train troops and plans for both war and defense — truly a ruler of great enterprise.

units.zh: 然使命不通，難保其不為寇。
units.en: Yet if envoys do not go and come, we cannot be sure they will not raid.
units.literal: Yet if missions do not pass, it is hard to guarantee they will not raid.

units.zh: 宜敕沿邊守臣，發兵遊僥，有警則入保，無事則力耕。
units.en: Your Majesty should order frontier commanders to patrol: in alarm they should withdraw to strongholds, in peace they should farm hard.
units.literal: Your Majesty should order frontier commanders to send out patrols; when there is alarm they should enter fortified places, and when there is peace they should farm with all their strength.

units.zh: 陛下於機務之暇，時召京營總督、總兵，詢以方略，誠接而禮貌之，信賞罰以持其後，斯戰守可言也。」
units.en: In moments free from urgent business, summon the capital camp commanders, ask their plans, treat them with sincere courtesy, and back them with sure rewards and punishments — then war and defense may be discussed."
units.literal: In Your Majesty's spare moments from state affairs, from time to time summon the metropolitan camp governors and commanders-in-chief, inquire into strategy, receive them sincerely with courtesy, and hold reward and punishment in trust behind them — then war and defense can be spoken of."

units.zh: 帝曰「善」。
units.en: The emperor said, "Well said."
units.literal: The emperor said "Good."

units.zh: 明年正月進少傅。
units.en: In the first month of the following year he was made junior grand tutor.
units.literal: In the first month of the following year he was advanced to Junior Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 帝欲易太子。
units.en: The emperor meant to depose the crown prince.
units.literal: The emperor wished to replace the crown prince.

units.zh: 未發。
units.en: He had not yet announced it.
units.literal: The matter had not yet been announced.

units.zh: 會思明土知府黃矰以為請。
units.en: Then Huang Zeng, native-office prefect of Siming, memorialized asking for it.
units.literal: It happened that Huang Ying, native-office prefect of Siming, requested this.

units.zh: 帝喜，下禮部議。
units.en: The emperor was pleased and referred the matter to the ministry of rites.
units.literal: The emperor was pleased and sent the matter down to the Ministry of Rites for deliberation.

units.zh: 胡濙唯唯，文武諸臣議者九十一人當署名，直有難色。
units.en: Hu Ying gave vague assent; ninety-one civil and military officials who debated had to sign, and Wang Zhi looked troubled.
units.literal: Hu Ying assented vaguely; ninety-one civil and military officials who deliberated had to sign, and Zhi showed reluctance.

units.zh: 陳循濡筆強之，乃署，竟易皇太子。
units.en: Chen Xun dipped the brush and pressed him until he signed; the heir was changed in the end.
units.literal: Chen Xun dipped the brush and forced him — he signed, and in the end the crown prince was replaced.

units.zh: 直進兼太子太師，賜金幣加等。
units.en: Wang Zhi was made grand preceptor to the heir apparent as well, with extra gifts of gold and silk.
units.literal: Zhi was promoted to concurrent Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent with enhanced gifts of gold and silks.

units.zh: 頓足嘆曰：「此何等大事，乃為一蠻酋所壞，吾輩愧死矣。」
units.en: He stamped his foot and sighed, "What a great matter, ruined by a tribal chief — we should die of shame."
units.literal: He stamped his foot and sighed: "What a great affair, to be ruined by a barbarian chieftain — we ought to die of shame."

units.zh: 景帝疾亟，直、濙等會諸大臣臺諫，請復立沂王為皇太子，推大學士商輅草疏。
units.en: When the Jingtai emperor was critically ill, Wang Zhi and Hu Ying met ministers and censors to ask that the Prince of Yi be made heir again, asking Grand Secretary Shang Lu to draft the memorial.
units.literal: When Emperor Jing was gravely ill, Zhi, Ying, and others met the great ministers and censorial officials and asked to restore the Prince of Yi as crown prince, entrusting Grand Secretary Shang Lu to draft the memorial.

units.zh: 未上，而石亨、徐有貞等奪門迎上皇復位，殺王文等。
units.en: Before it was submitted, Shi Heng and Xu Youzhen seized the gate to restore Yingzong and killed Wang Wen and others.
units.literal: Before it was submitted, Shi Heng, Xu Youzhen, and others seized the gate to welcome the retired emperor back to the throne and killed Wang Wen and the rest.

units.zh: 疏草留姚夔所，嘗出以示郎中陸昶，嘆曰：「是疏不及進，天也。」
units.en: The draft stayed with Yao Kui; he once showed it to director Lu Chang and sighed, "That this memorial was not submitted in time was Heaven's doing."
units.literal: The draft remained with Yao Kui; he once showed it to Director Lang Lu Chang and sighed: "This memorial was not submitted in time — Heaven's will."

units.zh: 直遂乞休。
units.en: Wang Zhi then asked to retire.
units.literal: Zhi then asked to retire.

units.zh: 賜璽書、金綺、楮幣，給驛歸。
units.en: He received a sealed letter, gold brocade, and paper money, with an imperial courier home.
units.literal: He was granted a sealed letter, gold brocade, and paper currency, and given an express post for his return.

units.zh: 直為人方面修髯，儀觀甚偉。
units.en: Wang Zhi had a square face, long beard, and imposing presence.
units.literal: Zhi was square-faced with a long beard and very imposing in bearing.

units.zh: 性嚴重，不茍言笑。
units.en: He was grave and seldom jested.
units.literal: His nature was grave; he was not casual in speech or laughter.

units.zh: 及與人交，恂恂如也。
units.en: Yet in company he was respectful and mild.
units.literal: Yet in dealing with others he was respectful and mild.

units.zh: 在翰林二十余年，稽古代言編纂紀註之事，多出其手。
units.en: For more than twenty years in the Hanlin he handled most work of historical research, drafting, compilation, and annotation.
units.literal: More than twenty years in the Hanlin, he handled most matters of antiquarian research, imperial drafting, compilation, and annotation.

units.zh: 與金溪王英齊名，人稱「二王」，以居地目直曰「東王」，英曰「西王」。
units.en: He was famed with Wang Ying of Jinxi as the "Two Wangs," Zhi called the Eastern Wang and Ying the Western Wang from where they lived.
units.literal: He was famed alongside Wang Ying of Jinxi; people called them the "Two Wangs," calling Zhi the "Eastern Wang" and Ying the "Western Wang" by their residences.

units.zh: 直以次當入閣，楊士奇不欲也。
units.en: By seniority Wang Zhi should have entered the Grand Secretariat, but Yang Shiqi did not want him there.
units.literal: By seniority Zhi should have entered the Grand Secretariat, but Yang Shiqi did not wish it.

units.zh: 及長吏部，兼廉慎。
units.en: As long head of the ministry of personnel he was also frugal and careful.
units.literal: When he long headed the Ministry of Personnel he was also frugal and cautious.

units.zh: 時初罷廷臣薦舉方面大吏，專屬吏部。
units.en: Court recommendation of regional governors had just ended; appointment rested solely with the ministry of personnel.
units.literal: At that time court recommendation of great regional officials had just been abolished, and appointment was entrusted solely to the Ministry of Personnel.

units.zh: 直委任曹郎，嚴抑奔競。
units.en: Wang Zhi relied on bureau directors and strictly curbed frantic office-seeking.
units.literal: Zhi entrusted the bureau directors, strictly suppressing frantic competition for office.

units.zh: 凡御史巡方歸者，必令具所屬賢否以備選擢，稱得人。
units.en: Whenever a touring censor returned, he required lists of the capable and incapable in his circuit for promotion — he was said to choose men well.
units.literal: Whenever a censor returned from regional inspection, he required a report on the worthies and unworthies under his jurisdiction to prepare selection and promotion — he was said to have chosen men well.

units.zh: 其子資為南國子博士。
units.en: His son Zi was a doctor at the Southern Directorate of Education.
units.literal: His son Zi served as a doctor of the Southern Directorate of Education.

units.zh: 考績至部，文選郎欲留侍直，直不可，曰：「是亂法自我始也。」
units.en: When his son's review reached the ministry, the appointments director wished to keep him at Wang Zhi's side; Wang Zhi refused, saying, "To break the law would begin with me."
units.literal: When his performance review reached the ministry, the appointments director wished to keep him to attend on Zhi; Zhi would not allow it, saying: "To disorder the law would begin with me."

units.zh: 朝廷以直老，命何文淵為尚書佐之。
units.en: The court, finding Wang Zhi aged, appointed He Wenyuan minister to assist him.
units.literal: The court, considering Zhi old, appointed He Wenyuan minister to assist him.

units.zh: 文淵去，又命王翺，部遂有二尚書。
units.en: When He Wenyuan left, Wang Hao was appointed, and the ministry had two ministers.
units.literal: When Wenyuan left, Wang Hao was appointed, and the ministry then had two ministers.

units.zh: 直為尚書十四年，年益高，名德日益重。
units.en: Wang Zhi was minister for fourteen years; as he aged his fame and virtue grew heavier.
units.literal: Zhi served as minister for fourteen years; as he grew older his reputation and virtue weighed ever more heavily.

units.zh: 帝優禮之，免其常朝。
units.en: The emperor honored him and excused him from regular court attendance.
units.literal: The emperor treated him with special favor and exempted him from regular court attendance.

units.zh: 比家居，嘗從諸佃仆耕蒔，擊鼓歌唱。
units.en: At home he sometimes farmed with tenant laborers, beating drums and singing.
units.literal: When he was at home he would farm and plant with tenant laborers, beating drums and singing.

units.zh: 諸子孫更叠舉觴上壽，直嘆曰：「曩者西楊抑我，令不得共事。
units.en: Sons and grandsons offered toasts in turn; Wang Zhi sighed, "Long ago Western Yang kept me out of the Grand Secretariat.
units.literal: Sons and grandsons in turn raised cups to wish him long life; Zhi sighed: "Formerly Western Yang kept me down and would not let me serve in the Grand Secretariat together.

units.zh: 然使我在閣，今上復辟，當不免遼陽之行，安得與汝曹為樂哉！」
units.en: Yet had I been in the cabinet when the present emperor was restored, I could not have escaped banishment to Liaoyang — how could I enjoy this with you!"
units.literal: Yet if I had been in the cabinet when the present emperor was restored, I could not have escaped exile to Liaoyang — how could I enjoy this leisure with you!"

units.zh: 天順六年卒，年八十四。
units.en: In Tianshun six he died, aged eighty-four.
units.literal: In the sixth year of Tianshun he died, aged eighty-four.

units.zh: 贈太保，謚文端。
units.en: He was posthumously made grand guardian with the posthumous title Wenduan.
units.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian with the posthumous name Wenduan.

units.zh: 秶仕至翰林檢討，亦以學行稱。
units.en: Zi rose to Hanlin reviser and was also praised for learning and conduct.
units.literal: Zi rose to Hanlin reviser, also famed for learning and conduct.

units.zh: 曾孫思，自有傳。
units.en: His great-grandson Si has his own biography.
units.literal: His great-grandson Si has his own biography.

units.zh: 贊曰：高谷之清直，胡濙之寬厚，王直之端重，蓋皆有大臣之度焉。
units.en: The commentator says: Gao Gu's purity and uprightness, Hu Ying's generosity, and Wang Zhi's dignity all showed the stature of great ministers.
units.literal: The commentator says: Gao Gu's purity and uprightness, Hu Ying's generosity and mildness, and Wang Zhi's dignity and gravity — all had the measure of great ministers.

units.zh: 當英、景之間，國勢初更，人心觀望，執政任事之臣多阿意取容。
units.en: Between Yingzong and Jingtai, when the realm's situation had just changed and people watched and waited, many ministers who held power and handled affairs flattered to please.
units.literal: Between the Ying and Jing reigns the national situation was newly changed and people's hearts were watchful; many ministers who held power and handled affairs flattered to please.

units.zh: 而谷、濙惓惓於迎駕之儀，直侃侃於遣使之請，皆力持正議，不隨眾俯仰，故能身負碩望，始終一節，可謂老成人矣。
units.en: Yet Gao Gu and Hu Ying were earnest over welcome rites for the emperor, and Wang Zhi was forthright on sending envoys — all held to right positions and did not bend with the crowd; thus they bore great weight and kept one principle to the end — true elders of the state.
units.literal: Yet Gu and Ying were earnestly devoted on the rites of welcoming the imperial carriage, and Zhi spoke forthrightly on sending envoys — all forcefully upheld correct positions and did not follow the crowd in bowing and rising; therefore they bore great weight in person and kept one principle to the end — they may be called men of mature judgment.
